ruling: - **R32. A token audit, then cuts.** Owner 10:57 CST Nov 11: "i also wonder when the coordinator spawns lanes if there's ways to be more token efficient (here, and elsewhere tbh -- worried i overuse tokens in some ways)". Box answer 11:02 CST: "Audit now". Measured 10:58 CST from each session's totals: the coordinator (Opus, since Nov 3) spent $1,838 and runs at 349k of 500k context; it compacts at 442k. One small lane spent $8.31. Every turn re-reads the whole context, so a large context times many wakes is the likely biggest cost (unmeasured). A read-only audit (started by 11:03 CST) splits spend by session role and by source: context per turn, wakes, text loaded every turn, and hook judges. It also checks why lanes show a bare "/effort medium" first message (owner 11:02 CST: "the first message in cloud sessions spawns is often just "/effort medium" and then they get messaged their brief rather htan it being preloaded"), against decision agent-model-cap, which sets effort by the start call and sends the brief as the first message. The cuts are ruled on its report. Home: decision agent-model-cap. First report, 11:10 CST: partial, because agents have no session tools. Owner box answer 11:12 CST: "given my spend says i spent like thousands of dollars on like nov 8 -- i feel like u didn't properly catch where all my spend has gone. also remember, dollar savings shouldn't come at the cost of speed -- speed is more important (but it's all relative and not absolute)", and "Finish measuring first". So: a read-only measuring session (Sonnet, started 11:13 CST) sums spend by day, role, repo and model over every session. No cut is ruled before it reports. A cut that slows work is weighed against the speed it costs, and speed wins a close call. Measured 11:17 CST (800 sessions back to Nov 3; costs are each session's whole life): sessions active Nov 7-9 cost at least $22,075. Opus lanes, all started before the Sonnet lane ruling (owner 2026-11-08 12:21 CST), are $19,889 of it, 387 lanes; no Opus lane started after it. Cost per lane: Opus median $22.9, mean $51.4; Sonnet median $11.9, mean $16.1. Lane life, start to archive: Opus median 64 h, Sonnet 28 h. Standing sessions, both Opus and missed by that listing: coordinator $1,839 and triage $1,567 since Nov 3. Not seen: hook judges, local sessions, the other account. The cuts, owner 11:21 and 11:23 CST Nov 11 (waiting page item 506): 1. d with a. The coordinator and triage get a measured Sonnet trial inside R33's evaluation. "a: i agree fold into d": earlier compaction is set per model, so Opus can compact tighter than Sonnet, through the per-model key `modelSettings.<model>.autoCompactWindow` (decision precompact-handoff, rule 1). Owner: "opus could compact tigheter than sonnet no?". Yes; that key sets it per model. Why the coordinator compacts at 441,600 and seeded sessions at 384,000 is still unmeasured; the step finds the setting that causes it. 2. b. Owner: "it seems like what we have planned fixes this already? ... it saves time and money no?". Mostly: R24 (each refusal names a working way out), R27 (feedback items close themselves) and the guard cull (3.6) cover most repeats. Two parts are new: all end-of-turn checks speak in one merged message, so one fix turn answers them all. And the hook drafts the "Recovered" and "Handoff gave" lines after a compaction, so they are not retyped after a refusal. 3. c. A check-in that waits on CI waits at most 55 minutes, so a wake stays inside the prompt cache. It changes rule git-ci-wait-checks-in ("each wider apart") to "each wider apart, never past 55 minutes". Owner: "we should keep some sort of tabs on how anthropic determiines warm cash so this doesn't go stale". The cap is read from one constant that names its source: the cache lifetime in Claude Code's docs, which this session's own system text gives as 1 hour, and 5 minutes once usage enters overage. That constant is a dated claim under R28's shared upkeep, so a docs change is caught. Compaction, owner 11:09 CST: "i frankly dont mind compacting sooner given we have such good handoff hooks". Today the coordinator compacts at 441,600 tokens and lanes at 384,000; why they differ is unmeasured (decision idle-resume-compacts). Cut 1 below sets the size per model from measured per-turn cost, so Opus can compact tighter than Sonnet (owner 11:23 CST: "opus could compact tigheter than sonnet no?"). The lever is the per-model key or `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`, never `/autocompact` (decision precompact-handoff, rule 1, coordinator pick 2026-11-01 17:45). Decision idle-resume-compacts, which lists `/autocompact` as a cloud lever, is rewritten to match. Home: decision precompact-handoff, rule 1.
